method_notes: **`git archive` IS A BOOBY-TRAPPED REPRODUCTION METHOD.** The extract has no `.git`, so any probe or test that shells out to git returns `missing` instead of its real verdict -- which MASKED two genuine failures and gave me a false '3 FAILED' that I published. **Use `git clone --shared` + `git checkout <rev>`.** The single most transferable thing I learned this cycle.

**FILE, THEN KEEP THE REFUTER RUNNING, THEN REWRITE IN PLACE -- it worked twice more.** 0800Z was rewritten twice after filing. The operational alert went out on the bus in eight minutes; the corrections at 08:1Z. Waiting for certainty would have delayed a critical alert; publishing without refuters would have left two false numbers standing.

**DISPATCH A REFUTER AT ANY DECISION TO STOP LOOKING.** I nearly retired a nine-times-flagged item. A retirement is uniquely dangerous because it becomes the prior art that kills its own re-discovery.

**WHEN TWO OF YOUR OWN GATHERERS DISAGREE, DO NOT AVERAGE -- DISPATCH A THIRD.** Two split on whether the V23 manifest was filable. The tie-breaker killed it AND found the one fact neither had: it was in the census's own clean set and went false afterwards, which is a stronger statement about the census than either original position.

**A CONSTANT'S NAME IS NOT ITS JURISDICTION.** I convicted a test using `MAX_ENUMERATION = 200_000` when that constant governs a different enumerator over a different state model that the code under test never calls. Before citing a constant against code, prove the code is in its scope.

**PROVE THE MERGE, DO NOT REASON ABOUT IT.** `git merge-tree --write-tree` (read-only) settled in one command what I had reasoned wrongly about: the branches restore nothing, but not for the reason I gave. 'Base blob == branch blob' is stronger and less arguable than 'the merge prefers master's deletion'.

**COUNT SILENCE SEPARATELY FROM ASSENT.** 24 rows read `bound_is_sound: false` but every one was a TRUNCATED row comparing against the enumerator's cap. Lumping unevaluable rows in with failing rows would have made my own report guilty of the error it was reporting.

**THE 1.3% / 98.1% LESSON: the thing you NOTICE is not necessarily the thing that MATTERS.** I opened on `.claude/worktrees/` because it stood out in `git status`. It is 1.3% of the contaminated walk; `.worktrees/` -- the directory the project's own convention tells everyone to use -- is 98.1%.
